A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TCA research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material and identifying the new checklist and appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original semi-synthetic experiments using IST and MIMIC-III, including benchmark results, confounder-strength and prompting studies, and demographic subgroup analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds a comparison against a text-based DR-learner in Table 5.

M1.justification: Sections 4–5 and Algorithm 1 retain the same nuisance estimation, doubly robust pseudo-outcomes, LLM-generated text surrogates, text embeddings, regression objective, and inference procedure. The new DR-learner comparison does not modify TCA.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same IST and MIMIC-III treatment-effect tasks, with the same demographic groups, confounder-strength scenarios, and prompt families. The added DR-learner comparison uses the existing datasets.

E2.justification: v2 adds TBE-DR, a standard DR-learner combined with the text-generation pipeline, as an evaluated comparator in Table 5. The existing TBE-S-learner, TBE-T-learner, TBE-TARNet, and TBE-CFR comparisons remain.

E3.justification: The varying-LLMs experiment changes its reported generator from GPT-3 in v1 to GPT-3.5 Turbo in v2. This revises a stated experimental setting, although unchanged Table 4 values do not establish that experiments were rerun. Other documented metrics, budgets, and data-generation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The new TBE-DR comparison tests whether TCA's advantage persists when the comparator also uses doubly robust estimation and the same text-generation setup. This provides a limited additional analysis of the confounding adjustment's contribution. Existing sensitivity and subgroup analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five runs and use mean ± standard deviation. Table 5 follows this existing practice, and the subgroup caption now explicitly repeats it. No new seed information, uncertainty-estimation procedure, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports TBE-DR PEHE of 0.187 ± 0.03 on IST and 0.266 ± 0.02 on MIMIC-III, compared with retained TCA values of 0.116 ± 0.02 and 0.179 ± 0.02. Earlier benchmark, subgroup, and sensitivity results remain unchanged, including Table 4's numbers despite its revised LLM description.

T1.justification: The estimand definitions, Assumptions 3.1–3.2, bias and identification lemmas, double-robustness result, and Appendix B proofs are unchanged. No new mathematical result or derivation accompanies the additional comparison.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: formalizing inference-time text confounding, proposing TCA for unbiased treatment-effect estimation, and demonstrating its effectiveness. The additional comparison supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the TBE-DR comparison as evidence that the advantage comes from confounding adjustment rather than choosing a DR-learner, and states that other meta-learners could be used in the final step. The existing limitations discussion is retained as Appendix F, formerly Appendix E.

D1.justification: New Appendix E documents ChatGPT Edu access, a Business Associate Agreement application, and the described zero-data-retention configuration. Conversely, Appendix C replaces the exact gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18 identifier with GPT-4o mini, reducing version specificity. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware, timing, and code-link disclosures remain.

R1.justification: The bibliography and related-work sections are retained, but the new DR-learner discussion sharpens positioning relative to the already cited method [33]: the claimed innovation is the confounding-adjustment framework rather than DR estimation itself.

P1.justification: v2 adds Setup and Results subsections, a NeurIPS checklist, and an additional acknowledgment appendix, alongside limited wording and conference-header edits. The original narrative and appendix text are largely retained rather than extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 5, relocates and swaps the numbering of the benchmark and subgroup tables, and adjusts figure placement and sizing. Figure 3(a)'s incorrect prompt-strategy caption is corrected to confounder strengths. Existing plots and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens the evidence with a previously missing DR-learner comparison under shared text-generation settings, helping distinguish the benefit of confounding adjustment from estimator choice. It also corrects Figure 3(a)'s misleading caption. These are useful but limited gains because the method, theory, coverage, and earlier results remain unchanged. Removing the exact GPT-4o mini snapshot slightly weakens reproducibility specificity but does not outweigh the added comparative evidence.
